best_for: Players who loved Transport Tycoon Deluxe and want it free on a current PC or Mac, with bigger maps, online multiplayer and a large library of community add-ons.
description:
OpenTTD is a transport business game made by the OpenTTD Team, whose copyright runs from 2005. It stays close to Chris Sawyer's original game and adds a long list of new features, many inspired by the TTDPatch fan project.

You lay track, build roads, airports and stations, and dig canals with ship lifts and aqueducts to carry boats over hills. Trains can run on electrified rail, monorail or maglev, and presignals and path signals help busy lines flow. You can build on slopes and coasts, and even bribe the town council. The game is translated into more than 50 languages, and you can pick a stable, testing or nightly build if you want to try new features early.

points.title: Free, with no original game needed
points.text: OpenTTD is a free, open-source remake of Transport Tycoon Deluxe under GPL 2.0. You do not need the old game: the free OpenGFX graphics set can be fetched on first run.

points.title: Own the original? Use its art
points.text: If you own Transport Tycoon Deluxe, you can copy its data files into the baseset folder and play with the original graphics, sound and music. The project cannot hand out those files.

points.title: Sound and music are a separate step
points.text: Sound and music sets are optional. OpenSFX and OpenMSX install from the in-game content menu, which also handles most community add-ons such as new vehicles and scenarios.

points.title: Play together online
points.text: You can run a company with friends or compete against them, in co-op or head-to-head games over the network.

points.title: Old saves keep working
points.text: Each new release is built to load savegames from older ones, and the team treats a failed load as a bug. That makes it safe to update in the middle of a long game.

points.title: Builds for almost every PC
points.text: Windows has x86, x64 and Arm64 installers that install for all users and need Windows 8 or later (Arm64 needs Windows 10). The Mac build is universal for Intel and Apple Silicon. On Linux the Flathub build covers x64 and Arm64 but is not marked as verified by Flathub.

points.title: Also free on Steam and GOG
points.text: If you prefer a store that updates for you, OpenTTD is free on Steam, GOG.com and the Microsoft Store.

points.title: Rolling back
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 17 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current release, so downgrades there need the project's own downloads.
